items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: but the phonograph records, which were all ad hoc kind of orchestras — Andre Kostelanetz, Percy Faith, those were typical of the upper end of things you might say

ctx.x: And you had top guys playing on the sessions, right?

Well yeah. Well now you’re getting into the studio scene in New York, which I was lucky enough to get into in the 1950s and stayed with into the 1980s. There were several hundred, as I estimate, it couldn’t have been more than maybe two hundred people who did most of the recording work in New York and by recording I mean not only the commercials for dozens of producers around town, but the phonograph records, which were all ad hoc kind of orchestras — Andre Kostelanetz, Percy Faith, those were typical of the…
So if you were listening to Andrew Kostelanetz, and then you listened to Percy Faith —
